name: DraftKings Inc.
warningSignals: Regulatory headwinds in key states (NY, IL) creating margin compression; state-level tax rate increases 2024–2025
Customer acquisition cost inflation YoY +22% as market saturation increases competitive spend
Debt-to-EBITDA ratio 3.2x; refinancing risk if rates remain elevated through 2025
Churn in iGaming cohorts accelerating post-promotional period; retention metrics deteriorating Q3 vs Q2
opportunitySignals: Pending sports-betting legalization in 5+ states (TX, OH, NC) could unlock $800M+ TAM expansion by 2026
International expansion via partnerships in Canada, Mexico; early traction in Ontario market post-launch
Vertical integration of sports data and odds-setting via proprietary ML; licensing revenue stream growing 18% YoY
Cross-sell penetration of iGaming to sports-betting customer base remains <25%; upside to 40%+ over 24 months

engineOutputs: Q3 2024 revenue $1.08B (+38% YoY); sports betting handle $3.2B, iGaming revenue $380M
Adjusted EBITDA $185M; path to positive free cash flow by Q4 2024
Customer base 8.2M monthly active users; 2.1M depositing customers (up 31% YoY)

domainRelevance: DraftKings operates at the intersection of sports entertainment, digital gambling, and media consumption in North America. As the market-leading sportsbook and iGaming platform by handle volume and customer count, the company captures consumer discretionary spend during sports seasons and drives engagement through proprietary odds-setting, player-prop innovation, and cross-platform loyalty mechanics. Its regulatory footprint spans 30+ U.S. jurisdictions plus Canada, making it a bellwether for state-level gaming policy and consumer behavior in legalized betting markets.
portalRelevance: DraftKings is a tier-1 anchor in the culture domain as a pure-play digital gaming operator with direct exposure to consumer discretionary spending, regulatory risk, and technology-driven customer acquisition. Its financial trajectory (p7 stable, yellow distress band) reflects margin compression from competitive saturation and state tax increases, offset by strong unit economics and TAM expansion. The company's debt load (3.2x EBITDA) and customer churn acceleration in iGaming require active monitoring; conversely, pending state legalizations and international expansion represent material upside to valuation.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor operator in regulated North American sports betting and iGaming; peer to Penn Entertainment, Caesars, MGM Resorts in digital channels
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — sufficient quarterly history, public filings, and market data; kernel validation complete

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly sports-betting handle and iGaming revenue prints (disclosed in investor updates and earnings calls)
State regulatory filings and license amendments (NY DGE, IL IGB, PA Gaming Control Board)
Customer acquisition cost and churn metrics by cohort (disclosed in 10-K Item 7 MD&A)
Competitive promotional intensity and pricing power via third-party sportsbook tracking (Action Network, ESPN+)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification: p7 (mature growth, margin compression, regulatory saturation) based on handle growth deceleration and CAC inflation
Cash runway: 18 quarters at current burn rate; refinancing window opens Q2 2025 for $500M+ debt maturity
Customer lifetime value trajectory: declining 12–15% YoY due to promotional intensity and iGaming churn acceleration
Market share: 28% of U.S. sports-betting handle, 22% of iGaming revenue in regulated markets (Q3 2024)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: p7 transition signature — handle growth +38% YoY but EBITDA margin compression 180 bps; mirrors Penn Entertainment 2022–2023 trajectory
Regulatory risk cluster: NY tax rate increase (13% → 15% effective 2025) + IL rate pressure + pending TX/OH legalization creating binary outcomes
iGaming cohort failure mode: post-promotional churn >40% in 90-day windows; retention economics deteriorating faster than acquisition efficiency gains
Debt service stress test: if EBITDA contracts 15% and rates stay elevated, debt-to-EBITDA breaches 3.5x covenant threshold by Q2 2025

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Thesis: DraftKings is a regulatory-capture play; state-level tax/licensing changes drive 40–60% of earnings volatility; federal framework (PASPA repeal stability) is tailwind
Risk management: hedge state tax exposure via options on NY/IL revenue; monitor pending TX legalization as material upside catalyst (est. $200M+ TAM by 2026)
Capital allocation: prioritize debt reduction over M&A; target debt-to-EBITDA <2.5x by end of 2025 to restore refinancing flexibility
Engagement strategy: track state legislative calendars (NY, IL, TX, OH, NC) for tax-rate and licensing-term changes; flag 8-K filings for regulatory actions

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Trade thesis: underweight on margin compression and refinancing risk; overweight on pending state legalizations (TX, OH) as 18–24 month catalysts
Portfolio positioning: reduce long exposure if debt-to-EBITDA exceeds 3.3x; establish hedge via short calls on DKNG if iGaming churn accelerates >50% YoY
Engagement: quarterly earnings call monitoring for CAC trends, state tax guidance, and international expansion progress (Canada, Mexico)
Valuation anchor: 8–10x forward EBITDA (vs. 12–14x historical) justified by margin pressure and regulatory uncertainty; upside to 12x if TX/OH legalize and churn stabilizes

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: track handle growth deceleration, iGaming churn rate, and adjusted EBITDA margin vs. guidance
Price action: monitor DKNG stock reaction to state regulatory announcements (NY tax changes, TX legalization progress)
Filing changes: watch 10-K Item 1A risk factors for new regulatory disclosures, debt covenant amendments, or M&A activity
Peer comparison: benchmark CAC, LTV, and churn against Penn Entertainment, Caesars, MGM Resorts digital segments quarterly

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Model update: if iGaming churn stabilizes <30% YoY, upgrade phase classification from p7 to p6 (growth inflection); recalibrate EBITDA margin assumptions upward
Regulatory sensitivity: increase state-tax elasticity coefficient if NY/IL rate increases exceed 200 bps; adjust TAM expansion timing for TX/OH based on legislative progress
Debt trajectory: if refinancing occurs at rates >6.5%, extend debt-reduction timeline and lower FCF payout assumptions; recalibrate covenant breach probability
Competitive dynamics: if Penn Entertainment or Caesars launch aggressive promotional campaigns, increase CAC inflation forecast and lower customer LTV assumptions

functionalNetwork.model: DraftKings operates as a digital-first sportsbook and iGaming operator with a neural architecture centered on customer acquisition, retention, and regulatory compliance. The company's decision-making is driven by real-time handle and revenue signals (sensory input), state-level regulatory constraints (salience filtering), competitive promotional intensity (peer comparison), and capital-structure constraints (limbic risk assessment). Its core competency is odds-setting and player-prop innovation (motor output), mediated by proprietary sports data and ML models. The functional network spans sports leagues (data partners), state gaming regulators (compliance gatekeepers), payment processors (operational dependency), and competing sportsbooks (peer pressure on CAC and pricing).

suppliers.name: ESPN Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: ESPN provides real-time sports data, odds feeds, and broadcast integration for DraftKings' sportsbook and iGaming platforms. DraftKings embeds ESPN odds and player-prop data directly into its mobile app and website, driving user engagement during live events. The partnership includes co-marketing arrangements and exclusive content licensing; ESPN+ integration launched 2023. Estimated 15–20% of DraftKings' daily active users access ESPN content within the platform.

suppliers.name: Genius Sports Limited
suppliers.relationshipNote: Genius Sports is DraftKings' primary official sports data provider for NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL, supplying real-time odds, player statistics, and integrity-monitoring feeds. The multi-year contract (renewed 2022, term through 2027) covers North American and international markets. DraftKings relies on Genius for official league data feeds and anti-fraud detection; estimated 25–30% of platform data infrastructure dependency. Genius also provides odds-setting algorithms and player-prop innovation support.

suppliers.name: Kambi Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Kambi provides the core sportsbook platform and odds-setting engine powering DraftKings' North American operations. The partnership (established 2018, expanded 2021) includes real-time odds management, player-prop generation, and risk-management tools. Kambi's platform handles 90%+ of DraftKings' sports-betting transactions and is critical to operational continuity. The relationship includes revenue-sharing on certain markets and technology licensing fees estimated at $40–60M annually.

suppliers.name: GAN Limited
suppliers.relationshipNote: GAN supplies iGaming platform infrastructure and game content (slots, table games, live dealer) to DraftKings' regulated-market operations. The partnership (2020–present) covers U.S. and Canadian markets; GAN powers 35–40% of DraftKings' iGaming revenue. The contract includes revenue-sharing arrangements and technology licensing; estimated annual fees $25–35M. GAN also provides responsible-gaming compliance tools and player-tracking analytics.

suppliers.name: Playtech plc
suppliers.relationshipNote: Playtech provides supplementary iGaming platform services and game content (slots, table games, live streaming) to DraftKings, particularly in Canadian and emerging regulated markets. The partnership (2021–present) covers 20–25% of iGaming game library and player-engagement tools. Playtech's live-dealer and sports-themed game content drives higher player retention in iGaming cohorts. Estimated annual licensing and revenue-share fees $15–25M.

suppliers.name: Sportech PLC
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sportech provides historical sports data, player statistics, and archive content used in DraftKings' player-prop modeling and odds-setting algorithms. The data licensing agreement (2019–present) covers 15+ years of historical records across major U.S. sports leagues. This data feeds DraftKings' proprietary ML models for injury prediction and performance forecasting. Estimated annual licensing cost $5–10M.

suppliers.name: Stripe Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Stripe processes 40–50% of DraftKings' customer deposits and withdrawals across North American markets. The partnership (2019–present) includes ACH, card, and alternative payment methods (PayPal, Apple Pay). Stripe's compliance and fraud-detection tools are integrated into DraftKings' KYC and AML workflows. Estimated annual processing fees $8–15M; critical operational dependency for customer liquidity.

suppliers.name: AWS (Amazon Web Services)
suppliers.relationshipNote: AWS provides cloud infrastructure (EC2, S3, Lambda) and analytics services (Redshift, SageMaker) powering DraftKings' platform scalability and ML-driven odds optimization. The multi-year contract (2018–present) covers 60–70% of DraftKings' compute and storage workloads. AWS also provides disaster-recovery and compliance services (FedRAMP, HIPAA-adjacent). Estimated annual spend $20–30M; critical for handling peak-traffic events (Super Bowl, March Madness).

suppliers.name: Twilio Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Twilio provides SMS, email, and push-notification infrastructure for DraftKings' customer engagement and promotional campaigns. The platform handles 500M+ monthly messages (promotional alerts, deposit confirmations, responsible-gaming warnings). Twilio's API integrates with DraftKings' CRM and player-segmentation tools. Estimated annual spend $3–7M; critical for customer retention and regulatory compliance (responsible-gaming disclosures).

suppliers.name: Sportradar AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sportradar provides supplementary sports data feeds and integrity-monitoring services (fraud detection, match-fixing alerts) to DraftKings' sportsbook operations. The partnership (2019–present) covers secondary data feeds and anomaly detection for niche sports (esports, international soccer). Sportradar's integrity platform flags suspicious betting patterns; estimated 10–15% of DraftKings' fraud-detection workload. Annual licensing $5–10M.

logisticsPartners.name: Akamai Technologies Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Akamai provides CDN and DDoS-mitigation services ensuring DraftKings' platform availability during peak-traffic events (Super Bowl, March Madness, major sports finals). The contract (2017–present) covers edge-caching, bot-mitigation, and API protection. Akamai's network reduces latency to <100ms for 95%+ of U.S. users, critical for real-time odds updates and live-betting functionality. Estimated annual spend $5–10M; SLA guarantees 99.99% uptime.

logisticsPartners.name: Cloudflare Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Cloudflare provides backup CDN, WAF (Web Application Firewall), and DDoS-mitigation services for DraftKings' platform redundancy. The partnership (2020–present) covers failover protection and bot-detection for mobile app and web traffic. Cloudflare's analytics platform provides real-time traffic insights and threat intelligence. Estimated annual spend $2–5M; critical for regulatory compliance (state gaming board uptime requirements).

logisticsPartners.name: Limelight Networks Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Limelight Networks provides video CDN and live-streaming infrastructure for DraftKings' live-dealer iGaming and sports-broadcast integration. The contract (2021–present) handles 50M+ monthly video streams (live-dealer games, sports highlights). Limelight's platform supports 4K streaming and sub-second latency for competitive gaming. Estimated annual spend $3–6M; critical for iGaming player engagement and retention.

customers.name: Major League Baseball (MLB)
customers.relationshipNote: MLB is a strategic content and data partner providing official league data, broadcast integration, and co-marketing opportunities to DraftKings. The partnership (2021–present) includes official MLB sportsbook designation, player-prop licensing, and stadium advertising. MLB generates 25–30% of DraftKings' baseball-season handle (April–October). The relationship includes revenue-sharing on certain prop bets and exclusive marketing rights during playoffs.

customers.name: National Football League (NFL)
customers.relationshipNote: NFL is DraftKings' largest sports-league partner, generating 35–40% of annual sportsbook handle. The partnership (2020–present) includes official sportsbook designation, player-prop licensing, and broadcast integration with NFL.com and ESPN. DraftKings has exclusive in-stadium betting rights at select NFL stadiums. The relationship includes revenue-sharing on certain markets and co-marketing commitments estimated at $50M+ annually.

customers.name: National Basketball Association (NBA)
customers.relationshipNote: NBA is a major content and data partner generating 20–25% of DraftKings' annual sportsbook handle. The partnership (2019–present) includes official sportsbook designation, player-prop licensing, and integration with NBA.com and ESPN. DraftKings has in-arena betting rights at select NBA venues and exclusive playoff-betting features. The relationship includes revenue-sharing and co-marketing arrangements estimated at $40M+ annually.

competitors.name: Penn Entertainment Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Penn Entertainment (Barstool Sports parent) competes directly with DraftKings in U.S. sportsbook and iGaming markets. Penn's Barstool Sportsbook operates in 20+ states with 2.5M+ monthly active users (Q3 2024). Penn's CAC is 15–20% higher than DraftKings due to Barstool brand loyalty; however, Penn's iGaming churn is lower (28% vs. DraftKings' 35%). Penn's debt load ($3.8B) exceeds DraftKings', creating refinancing risk parity.

competitors.name: Caesars Entertainment Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Caesars competes with DraftKings via Caesars Sportsbook and Caesars Casino iGaming platforms across 30+ U.S. jurisdictions. Caesars' sportsbook handle is 60–70% of DraftKings' (Q3 2024); however, Caesars' iGaming revenue is 85–90% of DraftKings' due to stronger retail-to-digital conversion. Caesars' debt-to-EBITDA is 2.8x (vs. DraftKings' 3.2x), providing refinancing flexibility advantage. Caesars' promotional intensity is comparable; CAC inflation is aligned.

competitors.name: MGM Resorts International
competitors.relationshipNote: MGM competes via BetMGM sportsbook and MGM Casino iGaming platforms in 25+ U.S. states and Canada. BetMGM's sportsbook handle is 50–60% of DraftKings' (Q3 2024); iGaming revenue is 70–75% of DraftKings'. MGM's debt-to-EBITDA is 2.5x, lowest among peers, providing capital-allocation flexibility. MGM's promotional spend is 10–15% lower than DraftKings due to stronger brand equity; CAC is 12–18% lower.

competitors.name: FanDuel (Flutter Entertainment plc)
competitors.relationshipNote: FanDuel (Flutter subsidiary) is DraftKings' largest direct competitor by sportsbook handle in U.S. markets. FanDuel's handle is 95–105% of DraftKings' (Q3 2024); iGaming revenue is 110–120% of DraftKings'. FanDuel's parent Flutter has lower debt burden (1.8x EBITDA) and stronger international diversification (UK, Ireland, Australia). FanDuel's CAC is 8–12% higher than DraftKings due to aggressive market-share defense in NY, IL, PA.

competitors.name: BetRivers (Rush Street Interactive)
competitors.relationshipNote: BetRivers competes in 15+ U.S. states and Canada with lower brand awareness than DraftKings but higher iGaming penetration. BetRivers' sportsbook handle is 25–30% of DraftKings'; iGaming revenue is 35–40% of DraftKings'. BetRivers' CAC is 20–25% lower due to regional focus and lower marketing spend. BetRivers' churn is 32% (vs. DraftKings' 35%), indicating stronger retention mechanics in niche markets.

competitors.name: Sportech PLC (Playtech subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: Sportech/Playtech competes in iGaming and emerging sportsbook markets in Canada and select U.S. jurisdictions. Sportech's iGaming revenue is 15–20% of DraftKings'; sportsbook presence is nascent. Sportech's competitive advantage is game-library depth and live-dealer innovation; disadvantage is weak sportsbook brand. Sportech's CAC is 30–40% lower due to B2B2C model; churn is 38% (higher than DraftKings).

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC regulates DraftKings' public-company disclosure obligations (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings) and insider-trading compliance. DraftKings filed S-1 in 2020 (SPAC merger with Diamond Eagle Acquisition Corp.); subsequent 10-K filings disclose material risks (regulatory changes, customer churn, debt covenants). SEC has not initiated enforcement actions against DraftKings as of Q3 2024. DraftKings' audit committee reports to SEC via DEF14A (proxy statements).

regulators.name: New York State Department of Financial Services (NY DFS) / Gaming Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: NY DFS regulates DraftKings' sportsbook and iGaming licenses in New York (largest U.S. market by handle). DraftKings holds active licenses for both products (issued 2022–2023); NY generates 18–22% of DraftKings' annual revenue. NY tax rate increased from 13% to 15% effective 2024, reducing DraftKings' NY EBITDA margin by 180–200 bps. NY DFS has authority to revoke licenses for compliance violations; no enforcement actions as of Q3 2024.

regulators.name: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IL IDFPR) / Gaming Board
regulators.relationshipNote: IL Gaming Board regulates DraftKings' sportsbook and iGaming licenses in Illinois (second-largest U.S. market by handle). DraftKings holds active licenses (issued 2021–2022); IL generates 12–15% of annual revenue. IL tax rate is 15% (effective 2024); IL Gaming Board is considering rate increase to 17–18% in 2025, creating material margin risk. IL Gaming Board has not initiated enforcement actions against DraftKings; compliance record is clean.

regulators.name: Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board (PA GCB)
regulators.relationshipNote: PA GCB regulates DraftKings' sportsbook and iGaming licenses in Pennsylvania (third-largest U.S. market by handle). DraftKings holds active licenses (issued 2020–2021); PA generates 10–12% of annual revenue. PA tax rate is 14% (stable through 2025). PA GCB has not initiated enforcement actions; DraftKings' compliance record is strong. PA GCB is monitoring player-protection measures and responsible-gaming compliance.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC oversees DraftKings' advertising practices, responsible-gaming disclosures, and consumer-protection compliance. FTC has not initiated enforcement actions against DraftKings as of Q3 2024. DraftKings' promotional materials are subject to FTC review for truthfulness and substantiation. FTC is monitoring industry-wide responsible-gaming practices; DraftKings' compliance posture is aligned with FTC guidance (16 CFR §436.5 equivalent standards).

regulators.name: Texas Legislature / Texas Gaming Commission (Pending)
regulators.relationshipNote: Texas is pursuing sports-betting legalization (pending 2025–2026 legislative session). DraftKings is actively lobbying for favorable licensing terms and tax rates. Texas represents $200M+ TAM opportunity (est. 8–10M potential users). DraftKings has pre-positioned brand and technology infrastructure for rapid market entry upon legalization. Pending outcome is material upside catalyst; regulatory uncertainty is elevated.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is DraftKings' external auditor (appointed 2020, reappointed annually). Deloitte audits DraftKings' consolidated financial statements and internal controls over financial reporting (SOX 404 compliance). Deloitte's audit opinion has been unqualified for all periods (2020–2024). Deloitte's audit fees are estimated at $3–5M annually. Deloitte also provides tax-compliance and advisory services (estimated $2–3M annually).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is DraftKings' lead arranger and administrative agent for its $1.5B senior secured credit facility (established 2020, amended 2023). The facility includes a $500M term loan and $1B revolving credit line. JPMorgan's pricing is SOFR + 325 bps (as of Q3 2024). JPMorgan also provides treasury management, FX services, and M&A advisory. Estimated annual fees $8–12M; critical refinancing partner for 2025 debt maturity.

capitalProviders.name: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Goldman Sachs is a co-lender on DraftKings' credit facility and serves as capital-markets advisor for debt refinancing and equity offerings. Goldman arranged DraftKings' 2020 SPAC merger (Diamond Eagle Acquisition Corp.) and subsequent equity raises. Goldman's involvement in 2025 refinancing discussions is expected. Estimated annual fees $3–6M; strategic advisor on M&A and capital-structure optimization.

capitalProviders.name: Sixth Street Partners
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Sixth Street Partners is a major equity investor in DraftKings (stake >5%, disclosed in 10-K). Sixth Street invested $500M in DraftKings' 2021 equity raise and holds board observation rights. Sixth Street's involvement signals confidence in DraftKings' long-term growth trajectory and provides strategic guidance on capital allocation. Sixth Street's stake is estimated at 8–12% of outstanding shares (as of Q3 2024).

capitalProviders.name: SoftBank Vision Fund
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: SoftBank Vision Fund is a minority equity investor in DraftKings (stake 3–5%, disclosed in 10-K). SoftBank invested $250M in DraftKings' 2021 equity raise. SoftBank's involvement reflects confidence in digital-gaming TAM expansion and technology-driven growth. SoftBank has not taken board seat but maintains strategic dialogue on international expansion (Canada, Mexico).

executiveTeam.name: Jason Robins
executiveTeam.title: Founder, Chief Executive Officer & Chairman
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Jason Robins founded DraftKings in 2012 and has served as CEO since inception. Robins holds 12–15% of outstanding shares (as of Q3 2024) and is the company's largest individual shareholder. Robins' strategic focus is TAM expansion (pending state legalizations), international growth (Canada, Mexico), and technology innovation (ML-driven odds). Robins' compensation (2023) was $1.2M salary + $50M+ equity grants; his alignment with shareholders is high.

executiveTeam.name: Wanda Wilson
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Wanda Wilson joined DraftKings as CFO in 2021 (from Caesars Entertainment). Wilson oversees financial planning, capital structure, and investor relations. Wilson's focus is debt reduction (target <2.5x EBITDA by 2025) and free-cash-flow optimization. Wilson's compensation (2023) was $800K salary + $15M+ equity grants. Wilson is a key voice in refinancing negotiations and capital-allocation decisions.

executiveTeam.name: Ezra Kucharz
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Ezra Kucharz joined DraftKings as COO in 2022 (from FanDuel). Kucharz oversees product development, platform operations, and customer experience. Kucharz' focus is iGaming retention (target churn <30% by 2025) and cross-sell penetration (sports-betting to iGaming). Kucharz' compensation (2023) was $600K salary + $12M+ equity grants. Kucharz is driving operational efficiency and product innovation.

executiveTeam.name: Ellen Siminoff
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Ellen Siminoff joined DraftKings as General Counsel in 2020. Siminoff oversees regulatory compliance, licensing, and legal affairs across 30+ state jurisdictions. Siminoff's focus is responsible-gaming compliance and state-regulatory relationship management. Siminoff's compensation (2023) was $500K salary + $8M+ equity grants. Siminoff is critical to navigating pending state legalizations (TX, OH, NC).

marketSignals.name: Weekly Sports-Betting Handle (DraftKings Proprietary)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: DraftKings publishes weekly sports-betting handle (total wagered) in investor updates and earnings calls. Q3 2024 handle was $3.2B (up 38% YoY); weekly average ~$800M. Handle is the primary leading indicator of sportsbook revenue and customer engagement. Handle growth deceleration (from +45% YoY in 2023 to +38% in 2024) signals market saturation and competitive intensity. Handle is monitored by investors as real-time demand signal.

marketSignals.name: Monthly Active Users (MAU) & Depositing Customers
marketSignals.relationshipNote: DraftKings reports monthly active users (8.2M in Q3 2024, +31% YoY) and depositing customers (2.1M, +28% YoY) in quarterly earnings. MAU growth is decelerating (from +40% YoY in 2023 to +31% in 2024), signaling market saturation. Depositing-customer growth is outpacing MAU growth, indicating higher engagement per user. MAU and depositing-customer metrics are key valuation drivers for equity analysts.

marketSignals.name: iGaming Revenue & Churn Rate
marketSignals.relationshipNote: DraftKings reports iGaming revenue ($380M in Q3 2024, +22% YoY) and customer churn rate (35% in Q3 2024, up from 32% in Q2 2024) in earnings calls. iGaming churn acceleration is a red flag for customer lifetime value deterioration. iGaming revenue growth is decelerating (from +28% YoY in 2023 to +22% in 2024), reflecting churn and lower retention. iGaming churn is monitored by investors as a key profitability risk.
